column3: The Hebrew says the land was “sworn” to the fathers; BSB uses “promised.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has “I also said” and identifies those not driven out only as “them”; BSB has “now I tell you” and “these people.”
The Hebrew has singular “their voice”; BSB uses plural “their voices.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew coordinates Joshua dismissing the people and Israel going out; BSB makes the dismissal an “after” clause.
The Hebrew repeats “all the days” and Joshua’s name, and calls the great work singular; BSB uses “outlived him” and plural “works.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the work singular; BSB has plural “works.”
The Hebrew retains the image “in the eyes of the LORD.”
The Hebrew says “other gods” where BSB has “various gods.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the LORD”; BSB uses “Him.”
The Hebrew uses singular “hand” twice and separately narrates the plunderers plundering Israel.
The Hebrew separately names what the LORD spoke and what the LORD swore, repeating His name in both clauses; BSB gives only “as He had sworn.”
The Hebrew uses singular “hand”; BSB has plural “hands.”
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; BSB explicitly names Israel.
The Hebrew begins with plural “judges,” then changes to “the judge”; BSB begins with singular “a judge.” The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name three times.
The Hebrew leaves the people unnamed and calls their way singular; BSB names the Israelites and uses plural “ways.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “anyone from the nations”; BSB uses “any of the nations.”
The Hebrew ends explicitly “or not”; BSB leaves that alternative implicit.
The Hebrew joins leaving the nations, not driving them out quickly, and not giving them into Joshua’s hand; BSB makes delivery the means of immediate expulsion.
